text:
sara: Heads-up: multiple tenant restores from last night failed mid-transfer with KMS AccessDenied. Saw 6 failures between 02:10-03:40 UTC.
lee: Which key/sa? Any pattern (region/job type)?
rahul: Job group=restoreAggregator, region=eu-west1, principal=serviceAccount:restore@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com, key=tenant-shared-key. Logs show a grant was present initially then disappeared.
sara: Log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T02:12:07Z restore-agg-198 start decrypt grantToken=abc123 expires=2026-03-18T03:12:07Z
2026-03-18T03:12:08Z restore-agg-198 decrypt failed: AccessDenied: grant expired
```
lee: Oof. We rolled ephemeral grant TTL from 24h->1h in the hardening change last week to reduce blast radius (CL #2145). That will bite long-running restores.
rahul: Audit shows grant issuance and explicit expiration. @audit-bot can you paste the IAM/audit entry for grant creation?
audit-bot: grant.create recorded: user=lee@redwood.ai action=create_ephemeral_grant resource=tenant-shared-key grant_id=abc123 ttl=3600 created_at=2026-03-17T22:12:07Z
sara: So restores started before expire but continued after; the restore process didn't refresh/renew grants mid-flight.
lee: My bad, I thought most operations were <30m. We need either renew-on-long-ops or increase TTL for long restores.
rahul: Short-term fix: extend TTL for current in-flight restores and re-run failed restores. Lee, can you re-issue grants with a 6h TTL for running jobs?
lee: Re-issuing now. Command I used: 
```bash
# ephemeral grant with 6h TTL for restore service
gcloud kms grants create --key=tenant-shared-key --member=serviceAccount:restore@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --ttl=21600 --description="temp extend for in-flight restores"
```
ops-bot: grant-create success: grant_id=xyz789 ttl=21600 target=restore@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
sara: Retried restore-agg jobs after new grant -> 4/6 succeeded, 2 still failing (those had multipart chunks uploaded with missing encrypt-meta, returned invalid-cipher error).
rahul: Separate uploader bug. Action items: 1) short-term: create guardrail that disallows ephemeral TTL < 4h for principals used by long-running ops (lee). 2) add renewal mechanism to the restore worker to refresh grants if remaining TTL < 30m (rahul). 3) add CI/lint rule to PRs that touch key-grant TTLs to call out long-running job membership (sara). 4) add a periodic scan to find grants expiring in next hour for active jobs and alert (ops).
lee: I'll open a hotfix PR to increase minimum TTL and re-issue grants for pending restores.
rahul: I'll scope the renew-on-long-ops change; we should be careful about race with grant pruning. Plan: renew and log audit event, then mark for explicit removal when job completes.
sara: Also we must confirm no unencrypted objects were created during failed retries. I'll run a scan on recent uploads for missing encryption headers and tag any offenders.
audit-bot: policy.change recorded: user=lee@redwood.ai action=set_min_ephemeral_ttl resource=org/project note="min_ttl=4h for restore principals"
lee: FYI, I'll also add docs in runbooks about ephemeral grant behavior and list critical services that need extended TTLs: restore, archive-rehydrate, long-export.
rahul: Postmortem action: 1) Incident write-up with timeline + list of failed restores (sara). 2) Deploy renew-on-long-ops in next sprint with e2e test that simulates >2h restore (rahul). 3) Add uploader metadata validation to CI to prevent missing encrypt headers (sara).
sara: Filing INC-2026-0071 and attaching logs + audit entries. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
lee: Sorry about the disruption, learned a good lesson about TTLs.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0071 created by sara@redwood.ai assigned=eng-security priority=P2
